question: Does the exact neutral-charge identity imply that arbitrary regular superhorizon neutral-charge onset memory cannot be uniformly erased over a finite in-EFT conformal-time interval as k->0?
assumptions: regular long-wave branch: |theta|<=C_theta k^2 and |B|<=C_B with finite k-independent C_theta,C_B on [tau_i,tau_f]
for a relative-memory statement only: |I_khr(tau_i)|>=I_min>0 independent of k
proof_obligation: derive an absolute finite-time bound on |I_f-I_i|
derive a relative transfer bound when I_min>0
take k->0 without assuming a numerical production history
state precisely what this does not exclude
acceptance: A valid proof must use only the exact parent identity plus the stated regularity assumptions and must not infer a UV boundary prescription or a new propagating degree of freedom.
